data.name: Ark
data.gender_notes: Ark is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In the Bible, Ark is the name of the vessel that saved Noah and his family from the Great Flood. It symbolizes salvation, protection, and the covenant between God and humanity. The name Ark carries the meaning “Vessel of salvation” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Ark usually hope their child will grow to embody vessel of salvation and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of faith and God's promise to protect His people.
data.etymology: Ark belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Vessel of salvation.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ark total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The term "Ark" has been used metaphorically to represent a place of safety and refuge. For instance, an "ark" oftentimes refers to a spacecraft that preserves life during a catastrophic event. This usage alludes to the biblical story and emphasizes its cultural importance.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian symbolism, the Ark signifies hope, faith, and God's promise to protect believers during times of adversity. It embodies the idea that God provides a safe haven for His people and maintains a covenant with them. The Ark also exemplifies the importance of remaining faithful to God, and that He will always stand by His people.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Ark carries profound spiritual symbolism as it is rooted in Biblical tradition. biblical_reference.note: In the Old Testament, the Ark of the Covenant was a wooden chest that contained the Ten Commandments and represented the presence of God among the Israelites. It was later carried by the Israelites as they journeyed through the wilderness, and was eventually housed in the Temple in Jerusalem.
